Who we are

Founded by young people to give Luton something better to do.

NGS began in 2005 when a group of young people set out to tackle antisocial behaviour on their own streets with positive activities. Two decades on, we're still volunteer-led, and we still work hand in hand with families, schools and partners across the town.

  • 01Reducing anti-social behaviour
  • 02Providing skills and experience
  • 03Enhancing future prospects
  • 04Increasing participation and involvement
  • 05Improving health and well-being
Meet the team
"NGS didn't just keep us busy… it shaped my future."

Wasim joined NGS aged 10. The clubs kept him and his friends safe and busy, and opened doors they'd never have found alone. He went on to work for NGS and is now a teacher.

BackNGS / Pakistan & Kashmir Culture Festival
Flagship event · every summer

Pakistan & Kashmir Culture Festival

A free, family day out that fills a Luton park with food, fashion, music and heritage. Organised by NGS, it has grown in three summers into one of the town's biggest cultural celebrations, welcoming people from every background.

2026 highlights · tap the speaker for sound
2024

Wardown Park · Sat 10 August

The first festival, held for South Asian Heritage Month. Sponsored by Luton Rising, with Inspire FM, supporting Luton Foodbank.

The beginning
2025

Stockwood Park · Sat 23 August

A bigger new home at Stockwood Park and thousands more visitors, with dignitaries joining the celebrations.

New home
2026

Stockwood Park · Sat 15 August

Year three, with media partner Inspire FM. The Lord-Lieutenant and High Sheriff of Bedfordshire and the Deputy Mayor of Luton attended.

Celebrating Luton's young talent

Luton Youth Awards

Launched by NGS in 2025, the Luton Youth Awards shine a light on young people aged 13–19 whose achievements often go unseen, from top students and athletes to young carers and changemakers. Each ceremony brings families, schools, businesses and community leaders together at the Grand Royale Banqueting Hall.

2025Inaugural ceremony, 24 October (sold out)
202617 July, headline sponsor Barnfield College

About us

Built by the community, for the community

Next Generation Scheme started in 2005, when young people in Luton set out to tackle antisocial behaviour with positive activities. Twenty years on we are still volunteer-led, running youth clubs, holiday camps, mentoring, the Luton Boot Bank, the Pakistan & Kashmir Culture Festival and the Luton Youth Awards.

We work hand in hand with families, schools, local businesses and partners to give children, young people and the wider community opportunities to learn, grow and celebrate together.

Our priorities

The areas we champion and support

Some we've delivered ourselves over the years, others we back by partnering with local groups, schools and charities, always led by what Luton's young people and families need.

  • Youth spacesSafe, welcoming places to meet, make friends and try new things.
  • Education & studyBuilding confidence and helping young people do well at school.
  • Health & wellbeingHealthy eating, fitness and good mental health for all ages.
  • Outdoors & environmentGreen spaces, trips and environmental projects.
  • Sport & recreationTeamwork, fitness and friendships through sport.
  • Mentoring & careersRole models, life skills and routes into future careers.
  • Culture & heritageCelebrating the heritage and cultures of Luton's families.

Before you start
  • Under 18? Most roles need a parent or carer to agree.
  • Roles with children or vulnerable adults need a DBS check. The organisation arranges it, free.
  • Ask for a reference when you have helped for a while. Volunteering also counts for DofE, UCAS and your CV.
  • Ask whether travel or lunch expenses are paid.

Our part in NGS

SMR Digital designed and built this website and app from scratch, every page, form and feature, and looks after it day to day: new events, activities and discounts every week, updates, hosting and support.

We do it as part of our support for NGS, so more of the charity's time and money goes straight to young people in Luton.

  • Find help in Luton

About this project

The NGS website and app, by SMR Digital.

Everything here was designed, built and is managed by SMR Digital, to help NGS reach more young people in Luton, do more to help them, and spend less time on admin.

Built from scratch

No templates or page builders. The design, the code, the booking forms, the admin app and the hosting were all made for NGS, so it does exactly what the charity needs and loads fast on any phone.

Works like an app

For people: add it to the Home Screen and it opens like an app, with no app store download. Everyone always gets the newest version.

For NGS: one website for phones and computers, so there is only one thing to keep up to date.

Luton Boot Bank

For people: apply for free football boots, donate a pair, or find the nearest drop-off hub.

For NGS: applications arrive in one place, and the live boot counter shows funders exactly how many pairs have been rehomed.

Holiday camp booking

For people: parents book a place online in a few minutes, with health details and photo permission in the same form.

For NGS: every booking lands in the admin app, and children's details are deleted automatically after 12 months.

Luton Youth Awards

For people: anyone can nominate a young hero online, and past winners live in the Hall of Fame.

For NGS: nominations are collected and sorted in one list, ready for judging.

Find help in Luton

For people: free food, money, housing and someone-to-talk-to support near them, sorted by what is closest.

For NGS: the team can point anyone who gets in touch to the right help straight away.

Events, activities and discounts

For people: what's coming up in and around Luton, local fun activities and money off for young people, with filters for price, age and Muslim-friendly options.

For NGS: the site is useful every week, not just when NGS has an event on, so people keep coming back.

How can I help?

For people: three quick questions show volunteers, donors and businesses the best way to get involved.

For NGS: more of the right offers of help, with less back-and-forth.

Partners & supporters

For people: tap any logo to see who they are and what they have supported.

For NGS: a proper thank-you to every funder and sponsor, which helps when asking for support again.

Accessible to everyone

For people: bigger text, a dyslexia-friendly font, read-aloud, stronger contrast and other languages, all in one panel.

For NGS: the site works for more of the community it serves.

Simple to run

A simple admin app behind the site lets the NGS team update the boot counter, festival date, bookings, nominations and partners without touching any code. Safeguarding, privacy and data policies are built in.

Shared across Luton

The events, activities and discounts listings are run by SMR Digital from one central hub and updated every week. The same up-to-date listings can also be added to other charity, school and community websites, so more young people in Luton see what's on.

Getting through winter

Emergency food for people in crisis across Luton: free, confidential and non-judgemental. Here's how to get help, how to give, and tips to keep warm for less.

Get helpGive foodNewsWinter tips
12 tipsWinter tipsHow to stay warm, save money and look after the people you love this winter.

Need food? How to get help

  1. Speak to a referral agencyLuton Foodbank works with over 100 local agencies, such as Citizens Advice, schools, GP surgeries and children's centres. They'll talk through your situation and give you a foodbank voucher.
  2. Take your voucher to a foodbank centrePresent it at one of the distribution points across Luton and collect an emergency food parcel.
  3. Get advice tooAdvisers can help with problems around rent, debt, benefits and more, so you can move forward.
Confidential visitsUnbranded food bagsNo shame in asking

Not sure who can refer you? Call Luton Foodbank and they'll point you to the right agency. Children under 5? Your local children's centre or your school's family worker can also help.

Call 01582 725838EmailMore free help

Most-needed items

One extra item in your weekly shop makes a real difference.

  • UHT milk
  • Rice (500g)
  • Tinned meat
  • Tinned vegetables
  • Tinned fruit
  • Fruit juice (cartons)
  • Breakfast cereal
  • Rice pudding (tinned)
  • Custard (tinned)
  • Instant noodles
  • Soup
  • Baked beans
  • Tinned tomatoes
  • Tinned fish
  • Tinned pasta in sauce
  • Pasta sauce
  • Tea bags
  • Biscuits (single packs)
  • Sugar (500g)

Extra help this winter

Support you might be able to get, and who to call.

Warm Home Discount£150 off your electricity bill this winter for eligible households, for example on Pension Credit, Universal Credit or Housing Benefit. Most people get it automatically. Cold Weather Payment£25 for each 7-day spell of freezing weather if you get certain benefits. It's paid automatically. Priority Services RegisterFree extra help from your energy supplier if you're of pension age, have young children, a disability or a health condition. Ask your supplier to add you. Power cut? Call 105Free, from any phone, to reach your local electricity network. Smell gas? Call 0800 111 999The national gas emergency line, free and open 24 hours. Leave the property if you can. Last updated: 14 November 2026

1. Who we are

NGS Youth & Community is the trading name of Next Generation Scheme CIC (a community interest company, company number 16739908). We are the "controller" of the personal information described here.

Questions or requests about your data: email info@nextgenerationscheme.co.uk or call 07594 107633. Data protection is overseen by our directors, Lobia Begum, Asma Khan and Mohammed Tariq.

3. Children and young people

Many of our projects are for children. Bookings for under-16s are made by a parent or carer. We only collect what we need to look after children safely, we limit who can see it, and we delete it on the schedule above. We will not publish a child's photo or name (for example, as an award winner) without permission from a parent or carer.

4. Photos and video at events

We take photos and video at our events to share our work. We tell people at the event when filming is happening. If you or your child would prefer not to be photographed, tell a member of the team on the day, or ask us later to remove a photo and we will. For camps, you choose yes or no when you book. Read our full photo and video policy.

5. Email updates

We only send updates about our projects and events to people who have ticked the box to say yes, or told us directly. You choose which topics you hear about. Every email has an unsubscribe link, and you can also email us to stop. Booking confirmations and replies to your enquiry are not marketing, so you'll get those either way.

6. Who we share it with

  • Our website and email host (SiteGround), who store the data for us securely.
  • Luton Borough Council, which funds our holiday camps fully or partly, including through the Holiday Activities and Food (HAF) programme. For these places we share the child's name, age, school, postcode, place type (including free school meals eligibility) and attendance, so the council can check places reach the families who need them. We do not share medical details or photos with the council.
  • Other funders such as Active Luton. Where they need reports we give totals, and share personal details only when the funding terms require it.
  • Venues or first aiders at a camp or event, only what they need to keep people safe (for example, allergies).
  • Police, social care or other authorities where the law or a safeguarding concern requires it.
  • SMR Digital, who build and look after our website and may need to access it to fix problems.

We never sell your data or share it with other organisations for their own marketing.

7. Outside the UK

Our data is stored in the UK or European Economic Area. If you use the language button on our website, the page text is sent to Google Translate (Google, USA) to translate it. Our fonts load from Google Fonts. Our website, database and email are hosted by SiteGround. See our cookies section for what is stored on your device.

8. Keeping it safe

Only NGS staff and volunteers who need it can see your information, each with their own login and access limited to their role. Passwords for connected mailboxes are encrypted, every change is logged, and backups are kept for 30 days and then deleted. To stop spam, we briefly record the internet address (IP) that a form was sent from, and delete it within 24 hours.

9. Your rights

You can ask us to: see the information we hold about you; correct it; delete it; stop or limit how we use it; give it to you in a format you can reuse; or stop emailing you. Where we rely on your consent you can withdraw it at any time. Email info@nextgenerationscheme.co.uk. We will reply within one month.

If you're unhappy with how we've handled your data, please tell us first. You can also complain to the Information Commissioner's Office: ico.org.uk or 0303 123 1113.

10. Changes

We'll update this notice if the way we use data changes, and show the date at the top.

Our policies

How Next Generation Scheme keeps children and young people safe, uses photos, runs this website and protects your information.

Safeguarding children and young people

If a child is in immediate danger, call 999. If you are worried about a child, you can also call the NSPCC helpline on 0808 800 5000. Children and young people can call Childline on 0800 1111.

Next Generation Scheme works with children, young people and families across Luton. Everyone who takes part in our projects has the right to be safe, respected and listened to, whatever their age, background, ability, gender, race, religion or sexuality.

Who is responsible

  • Our directors are responsible for safeguarding and review this policy every year.
  • We name a Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) for the organisation, and a lead for each camp or event. Every volunteer is told who the lead is before they start.
  • To raise a concern with NGS, email info@nextgenerationscheme.co.uk with "Safeguarding" in the subject, or call 07594 107633.

How we keep children safe

  • Safer recruitment: staff and volunteers in roles with regular or unsupervised contact with children have an enhanced DBS check, references and a short induction.
  • Training: everyone working with children learns how to spot signs of abuse or neglect and what to do. Leads complete recognised safeguarding training.
  • Supervision: we keep safe staff-to-child ratios, never leave a volunteer alone with a child out of sight of others, and sign children in and out.
  • Health and safety: every camp and event has a risk assessment, a first aider and a record of allergies and medical needs, shared only with the people who need it.
  • Online safety: staff and volunteers do not contact children privately on social media or personal phones. Messages go to parents and carers, or through official NGS accounts.
  • Code of conduct: adults treat young people with respect, avoid favouritism, never use physical punishment, and report any behaviour that worries them.

What happens when there is a concern

  1. Listen to the child calmly, do not ask leading questions, and do not promise to keep a secret.
  2. Write down what was said and seen, in the child's own words, with the date and time.
  3. Tell the DSL or event lead the same day. If a child is at immediate risk, call 999 first.
  4. The DSL decides the next step and, where needed, refers to Luton Borough Council's children's services or the police. Concerns about an adult who works with children are reported to the council's Local Authority Designated Officer (LADO).
  5. Records are kept securely and shared only with those who need to know.

Photos and video

Photos and video help us show what our projects achieve, thank our funders and encourage more young people to take part. We take them with care.

  • Permission: for anyone under 18 we ask a parent or carer. For camps, you choose yes or no on the booking form. For other events, we ask before taking close-up photos of a child, and you can tell any team member on the day if you prefer not to be photographed.
  • No full names: we never put a child's full name with their photo. Award winners' names and photos are only published with permission from a parent or carer.
  • Where we use them: this website, NGS social media, printed leaflets and banners, reports to funders, and local media covering our events.
  • Taking photos: only NGS staff, volunteers or photographers we have briefed take official photos, using NGS equipment or accounts where possible. Photos are moved off personal devices and deleted from them after the event.
  • Never: photos of children changing, swimming, upset or in a way that could embarrass them.
  • Parents and visitors: you are welcome to photograph your own child at public events. Please don't share photos of other people's children online without asking.
  • Changing your mind: you can withdraw permission at any time. Email info@nextgenerationscheme.co.uk and we will remove the photo from our website and social media and stop using it in new material. We can't recall printed items already handed out.

Website terms of use

  • This website is run by Next Generation Scheme CIC. By using it you agree to these terms.
  • Information: we keep event dates, places and listings as accurate as we can, but details can change. Please check with us before travelling. The "Find help in Luton" listings are run by other organisations; check with them directly, and in an emergency call 999.
  • Bookings and forms: sending a form is a request. A camp place, stall or other booking is confirmed only when we email you to confirm it. Please tell us as soon as possible if you can no longer come, so the place can go to another family.
  • Using our content: the text, logos, photos and design on this site belong to NGS or the people who gave us permission to use them. You can share links and use short extracts to talk about NGS, but please ask before reusing photos or logos.
  • Other websites: links to partners and other sites are for your convenience. We are not responsible for their content.
  • Fair use: please don't misuse the site, for example by sending spam through our forms or trying to access areas you are not allowed to.
  • Liability: we are not liable for any loss caused by using this website, except where the law says we cannot exclude it.
  • These terms are governed by the law of England and Wales.

Cookies and your device

We don't use advertising or tracking cookies, so we don't need to ask before you browse. What we do store:

  • Language choice: if you use the language button, Google Translate stores a small cookie ("googtrans") so pages stay in your chosen language.
  • Small preferences: your browser remembers things like whether you've already seen the opening animation, and any accessibility settings you choose (text size, font, colours). This stays on your device and isn't sent to us.
  • Staff login: the NGS admin area uses one essential cookie to keep staff signed in. Visitors never receive it.
  • Website statistics: we count page views and button clicks without cookies, names or IP addresses.
  • Fonts: our fonts load from Google Fonts, which sees your IP address when the page loads, like any website server.

You can clear or block cookies in your browser settings at any time.

If something goes wrong with your data

A data breach means personal information being lost, stolen, seen by the wrong person or changed without permission. If this happens, NGS will:

  1. Stop it as quickly as we can, for example by recovering the information, changing passwords or removing access.
  2. Record what happened, what information was involved and who could be affected.
  3. Report it to the Information Commissioner's Office within 72 hours of finding out, where it could put people at risk.
  4. Tell the people affected without delay if there is a high risk to them, with advice on what to do.
  5. Review what went wrong and change how we work so it doesn't happen again.

If you think your information has been misused, email info@nextgenerationscheme.co.uk.
